about: The guide's own accessibility results on the Gate 2 preview after the fix pass and its second pass, printed by Rule 19.8 through stage_c_ch19_build.py. Written by the accessibility lead from the final runs named in 'runs', on the build named in 'build'. Each line states what ran and what it found; checks that did not run are in 'not_tested' with the reason. An item still open carries "open": true, which the page prints as “Open, to fix before launch.” None is open in these runs. Round 2's results stay as the record in 20261111_Stage-C-Round-2-Ch19-Results.json.

tested.result: axe-core 4.10.2 with the tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa found no violation at any of the four widths, with its color-contrast rule run outside the plates marked as contrast failures.

No text measured under 4.5 to 1, or 3 to 1 for large text, outside the labeled failure plates, and no text under 13 px, at all four widths. The token tests found every role that carries a contrast threshold at or over it on each surface it serves.

The first 60 Tab stops at 1440 and 390 px each showed a focus ring. All 37 keyboard paths of chapter 18’s 24 components and chapter 26’s download passed: 140 walks and 714 steps, in both themes at 1440 and 390 px. On the Where to start page every stop showed its ring in order at all four widths, and each of its 20 steps opened its place and returned to the step. Each Clear the search control that shows only after typing measured 44 by 44 px, and the masthead’s phone menu opened, held focus, closed by Escape and by Close, and returned focus, at 390 and 360 px.
272 headings with one h1, no skipped level and none inside a specimen, at every width.

Chapter 18’s form, walked by keyboard in both themes at 1440 and 390 px, kept the email field from reading as wrong while it was typed; sent with two mistakes, it moved focus to the first field to fix and marked both fields invalid; sent right, its button read “Sending” and its status line said the reader was signed up.

At the default text size no width scrolled sideways outside a scroll frame. With text at 200 percent at 1024, 390 and 360 px, and with WCAG’s text spacing at 390 and 360 px, the page did not scroll sideways and no control clipped its words.
All 7 moving specimens stayed still on load, came to rest after Play, and with reduced motion on showed their final frame at once.
With forced colors emulated at each width, 597 to 600 glyph parts kept their contrast, and the masthead’s wordmark drew in one color in the dark and the light palette.

With the device set to dark, all 68,337 elements kept their light colors, so the guide stays on Newsprint. No Pillar Red pixel sat within 2 px of a Prussian one in any of 489 stages at 1440 px, both themes of each live component included, and again after Send was pressed in 3 of 3 forms.

Each of the 28 code sets, pasted into a blank page with tokens.css, drew as its live stage in both themes at all four widths: 32 to 41 of the 56 stages pixel for pixel, the rest differing only at edges, within the measured tolerance, and a comparison of 2,154 elements’ computed styles found no difference.

Every Civic Line, pillar, fit and utility drawing in the page’s sprite drew as its master at 1x and 2x, with a largest difference of 0, and each of the 41 drawings that switch showed its 24 px fit alone at 1x and 1.5x and its master alone at 2x.
The page loads its three faces from the file itself: with the network shut at 1440 and 390 px, each face the check asked for loaded, and the page made no request for a font.

not_tested.why: This run saved no captures, and no one looked at every chapter at all four widths on this build.
No report exists yet; chapter 24 brings the first.
The check’s narrowest width is 360 px.
No run filled the components with the atlas’s longest titles.
The token download test was not among this build’s runs.
Not checked by script; chapters 14 and 15, which hold most drawings, are not written yet.

iPhone with VoiceOver, Android with TalkBack, Windows with NVDA and a contrast theme, and Mac with VoiceOver: the machine these checks ran on has none of them, and Rule 19.9’s script runs each before launch.
Every check ran in Chromium only.

not_tested.check: Keyboard order and reading order by a person
not_tested.why: Only scripts walked them on this build.
